data.title: Trifunctional PIP3 binder identification
data.projectDescription: Trifunctional PIP3 is a chemically modified derivate of PIP3 that includes 3 functionalized groups allowing spacial an temporal manipulation of its release and function. A caged group allows for timed release of the coumpound, a cross-linking group induces covalent binding to binders, while a clickable group is used for specific pull=out using functionilized beads. These functionalities comibend create a precise discovery tool used to detect PIP3 interactors.
data.sampleProcessingProtocol: 3x106 cells were seeded in 150 mm dishes, two dishes for each condition. Three conditions were selected: cells loaded with compound 1b exposed to UV light (+UV), cells loaded with compound 1b and not exposed to UV light (-UV), and cells not loaded with compound 1b. The cells were grown for 24 h in full media and then loaded with compound 1b (5 µM final concentration) in DMEM overnight. After exposure of cells to 400 nm UV light for uncaging for 2 min, the diazirine group was activated for cross-linking via exposure to 350 nm UV light for 5 min. Cells were then washed and scraped in 5 mL PBS, centrifuged for 5 min at 500 rpm and PBS was discarded. Cells fractions were then isolated using the MinElute plasma membrane protein isolation kit (Invent Biotechnologies, Cat No SM-005). The cytoplasmic and total membrane fraction (resuspended in PBS:0.5% Triton X-100) for each sample were incubated with 200 µl prewashed picolyl-azide agarose beads (Click Chemistry Tools, Cat No 1235, Component A) in presence of 1 mM final CuSO4, 100 µM BTTAA or TBTA and 1 mM sodium ascorbate to catalyze the click reaction (RT for 1 h agitating). The beads were then extensively washed in disposable PD-10 columns (full column volume of each buffer): 3x with PBS, 3x with 50mM ammonium-bicarbonate, 3x 50 mM ammonium-bicarbonate 3M urea and 3x with 50 mM ammonium-bicarbonate to remove unspecific binders. The beads were then transferred to a clean Eppendorf tube, spun down and resuspended in 500 µL 50 mM ammonium-bicarbonate/3 M urea. Bound proteins were reduced via the addition of 5 mM final TCEP and incubated at 55°C with orbital shaking for 30 min. Proteins were then alkylated with 10 mM iodoacetamide (final concentration) for 20 min, incubated at RT in the dark, followed by the addition of 20 mM final DTT for 10 min at RT with shaking. The beads were precipitated vie centrifugation and the supernatant was removed from the beads. The beads were resuspended in 150µl 50 mM ammonium-bicarbonate/2M urea. 3 µg of MS grade trypsin was added and incubated overnight at 37°C with vigorous shaking to prevent the beads from settling. In the morning 1µg fresh trypsin was added and incubated for additional 2h. The supernatant was saved and beads washed once with 250 µl 50 mM ammonium-bicarbonate/2M urea that was added to the previous supernatant containing digested peptides. The total supernatant containing the digested peptides was acidified with 0.5% TFA (final concentration). The peptides were purified on a C18 desalting column, and dried. Dried peptides were submitted to the EMBL proteomics core facility where they were analyzed by LC-MS/MS on an Orbitrap Fusion Lumos mass spectrometer (Thermo Scentific). Peptides were separated using an Ultimate 3000 nano RSLC system (Dionex) equipped with a trapping cartridge (Precolumn C18 PepMap100, 5 mm, 300 μm i.d., 5 μm, 100 Å) and an analytical column (Acclaim PepMap 100. 75 × 50 cm C18, 3 mm, 100 Å) connected to a nanospray-Flex ion source. The peptides were loaded onto the trap column at 30 µl per min using solvent A (0.1% formic acid). Peptides were eluted using a gradient from 2 to 85% Solvent B (0.1% formic acid in acetonitrile) over 120 min at 0.3 µl per min (all solvents were of LC-MS grade). The Orbitrap Fusion Lumos was operated in positive ion mode with a spray voltage of 2.4 kV and capillary temperature of 275 °C. Full scan MS spectra with a mass range of 300–1500 m/z were acquired in profile mode using a resolution of 120,000. AGC target was set to 50% and a max injection time of 250 ms. Precursors were isolated using the quadrupole with a window of 1.4 m/z and fragmentation was triggered by HCD in fixed collision energy mode with fixed collision energy of 30%. MS2 spectra were acquired with the Orbitrap with a resolution of 15.000. Normalized AGC target was set to 200% and a max injection time of 32 ms.
data.dataProcessingProtocol: Acquired data were analyzed using IsobarQuant (PMID: 26379230) and Mascot V2.4 (Matrix Science) using a reverse UniProt FASTA database (UP000005640) including common contaminants. The following modifications were taken into account: carbamidomethyl (C, fixed), acetyl (K, variable), acetyl (Protein N-term, variable), oxidation (M, variable). The mass error tolerance for full scan MS spectra was set to 10 ppm and for MS/MS spectra to 0.2 Da. A maximum of two missed cleavages were allowed. A minimum of two unique peptides with a peptide length of at least seven amino acids and a false discovery rate below 0.01 were required on the peptide and protein level (PMID: 25987413). The resulting dat files were analyzed using Scaffold 3. Average spectral count of each condition was calculated for each protein for the 3 repeats. The average spectral counts of +UV samples were compared to both -UV and control average spectral counts. Proteins with a ratio increase of 1.2 in both comparison (+UV/-UV and +UV/K) were considered for further analysis. To further decrease the number of proteins we discarded proteins that had variability higher than 20% between repeats for the same condition.
